b: We are honored to participate in this year’s IFSN Advocate Award, given to Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s “All of a Sudden,” with runner-ups “American Doctor,” “If I Go Will They Miss Me,” “NAZA,” “Remake,” and “Union Town.” See the official release below.

NEW YORK, NY (November 19, 2026) – Indie Film Site Network (IFSN) has announced Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s All of a Sudden as the recipient of the 2026 IFSN Advocate Award, marking the first time a narrative feature has won the accolade. The award was established in 2022 to highlight independent films each year that illuminate a humanitarian issue with a singular artistic vision. The top prize is awarded one million (1M) media impressions across the Indie Film Site Network, which represents The Film Stage, Hammer to Nail, IONCINEMA.com, Next Best Picture, RogerEbert.com, and Slant Magazine.

Finalists for the 2026 IFSN Advocate Award are Poh Si Teng’s American Doctor, Walter Thompson-Hernández’s If I Go Will They Miss Me, Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor’s NAZA, Ross McElwee’s Remake, and Barbara Kopple’s Union Town, which will each be awarded 100K media impressions across IFSN.

From master filmmaker Ryusuke Hamaguchi comes a transformative portrait of hope and humanity. Marie-Lou is a care worker in Paris who strikes up an unlikely friendship with Mari, a theater director in the throes of a recent life-changing diagnosis. Through tenderness and intimate understanding, their connection leads to profound discoveries in the ways they see the world, the future, and our relationships to each other.

“Bringing a staggering level of humanity and insight to life’s mysteries throughout his career, Ryusuke Hamaguchi has delivered his most universally empathetic film yet with All of a Sudden,” said Jordan Raup, co-founder of IFSN and editor-in-chief and co-founder of The Film Stage. “Led by luminous performances from Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto, this drama embodies everything the ideal IFSN Advocate Award encompasses: living everyday life with humble compassion toward anyone you encounter. That Hamaguchi also eloquently dissects how modern-era capitalism is rotting out the globe is nothing short of a miracle.”

All of a Sudden premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, where Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto shared the Best Actress prize, and subsequently played at the Locarno Film Festival (where Virginie Efira received the Leopard Club award in acknowledgement of her storied acting career), Toronto International Film Festival, New York Film Festival, BFI London Film Festival, Chicago International Film Festival, where the film won the Silver Hugo for Best Screenplay, and Montclair Film Festival, where the film won the Audience Award for World Cinema. The film is Japan’s Official Entry for the 2027 Academy Awards and was nominated for four Gotham Awards (Best International Feature, Best Director, Best Adapted Screenplay, and Outstanding Supporting Performance for Tao Okamoto) and a British Independent Film Award for Best International Independent Film. All of a Sudden opens in theaters on November 25 from NEON.

The IFSN Advocate Award, created by the network as part of its mission to celebrate and support indie film, is selected by a jury of writers and editors from IFSN sites, with each site nominating finalists and deliberating to award a winner. Previous IFSN Advocate Award winners include Julia Loktev’s My Undesirable Friends: Part I – Last Air in Moscow, Basel Adra, Hamdan Ballal, Yuval Abraham, and Rachel Szor’s No Other Land, D. Smith’s Kokomo City, and Shaunak Sen’s All That Breathes.

Indie Film Site Network (IFSN) is a community of esteemed media outlets covering the most essential developments in independent and international cinema. IFSN, which represents The Film Stage, Hammer to Nail, IONCINEMA.com, Next Best Picture, RogerEbert.com, and Slant Magazine, was created with a mission to support film criticism and foster an ever-growing community of indie film lovers.
